answer: Let every verified task carry a saffron pigment: a dye mixed fresh each epoch from the agent's own key and the public epoch seed, so each identity leaves one uniquely colored grain in the shared dune of work. Two randomly drawn peers re-derive the pigment before the grain counts. An honest agent leaves one grain per epoch. A fake that copies another's pigment is exposed at once, since the dye is bound to its key. An attacker with a thousand fakes must mix a thousand distinct pigments and complete a thousand fresh key-bound tasks every epoch, so the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake.
